## Create and select columns

In this milestone, you'll write some of the code that was written for you in milestone 2. This will familiarize you with the format of the events data.

In the chunk below the events_formatted.parquet file is read in, named "events", and filtered for health events. You can just add your code to this chunk in order to acomplish the tasks listed below the chunk.

You will recognize select helper functions like starts_with() and contains(). These are used to simplify your data so there are not so many columns to look at.

This data comes from a dairy comp report events/2 with several additional options and switches.

```{r}
events<-read_parquet(here::here('data/intermediate_files/events_formatted.parquet'))%>%
   select(location_event, 
         id_animal, 
         id_animal_lact,
         id, date_birth,
         lact_number, lact_group,
         event_type, date_event,
         dim_event, dop_event, starts_with('age'), 
          event, remark, protocols, locate_lesion,
         contains('event'), 
         contains('remark'), 
         contains('protocols') 
         )%>%
  filter(event_type %in% 'health')
  
#Add new variables using predefined functions

events <- fxn_add_event_counts(events)

events <- add_new_variables(events)
 
#List of events and comparison between event day of phase (dop_event) and days in milk (dim_event)

sort(unique(events$event))

#Filtering data frame to focus on udder health and creating categorical variable
df_udder_only <- events |>
  filter(
    startsWith(event, "MAST") | startsWith(event, "CULTURE"),
    lact_group != "Heifer"
  ) |>
  mutate(dop_event_cat = case_when(
    dop_event <= 21  ~ "Early_lactation",
    dop_event <= 150 ~ "Mid_lactation",
    TRUE             ~ "Late_lactation"
  )) 

#Quality check (missing values, categorical variable, list of events)

lapply(df_udder_only[, c("event", "lact_group")], function(x) sort(unique(x)))

df_udder_only |> 
  summarise(
    na_event = sum(is.na(event)),
    na_dop_event = sum(is.na(dop_event))
  )

df_udder_only |>
  group_by(dop_event_cat) |>
  summarise(
    min = min(dop_event, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(dop_event, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

event_counts_by_month <- df_udder_only |>
  distinct(event, floordate_month, dop_event_cat, id_animal) |>
  group_by(event, floordate_month, dop_event_cat) |>
  summarise(n_animals = n(), .groups = "drop")

df_udder_only |>
  mutate(difference = dop_event - dim_event) |>
  summarise(
    min_diff = min(difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_diff = max(difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_different = sum(difference != 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```


1.  add a pipe to filter `events` further so you only have only one or 2 unique health events that are interesting to you. The example in the solution is based on 'NAVEL' and 'SEPTIC' events, but choose anything you want. If it is not NAVEL and SEPTIC don't worry about the solutions not matching in this milestone.

2.  add a pipe to create a new variable named **floordate_month**. The logic to create this variable is: **floor_date(date_event, 'months')**

3.  add a pipe to the function fxn_add_event_counts(). This will add columns indicating the number of times the animal has had that event within the data set (event_count_animal) or within their lactation (event_count_lact). If you would like to see the code the creates these click on the function in your environment. Look at the data frame an check to see that the values in the new variables of event_count_animal and event_count_lact make sense. (hint: an easy way to do this is to look at a dataframe of only 1 animal and arrange it properly).  Are these counts logical?

4.  add a pipe and use mutate to create a new variable named `category_dop_event`.  This new variable should categorize the day of phase at the time of the event (dop_event). Your new variable should allow you to look at specific dop intervals for the event you are interested in. The cut points should be sensical based on your questions about the event you picked. If you prefer to use dim_event or age_event that is fine.

5. Create a new dataframe that uses the distinct() function to count the number of unique animals (id_animal) within each event and floordate_month, and category_dop_event.  Name this dataframe `event_counts_by_month`.

### Step 2 - Disease and Treatments

Look at the example graphic below the next chunk. Pay special attention to the x axis as well as the facet and fill variables.

Create 2 new variables for your events named: `Disease` and `Treatment`. Use case_when() and whichever columns you would like to create the most useful variables.  Notice that there are several options for columns that contain the information from Remark. Explore them and see if any are useful for your events.

Run the chunk below to see the example graphics. . . . your graphics can be prettier!

```{r}

knitr::include_graphics(('milestones_dairy/images/milestone4_disease_by_phase.jpg'))

#Create variables number of affected quarters, indicator variables for affected quarters, and treatment (locate_lesion already interpreted remark)
 
df_mastitis_only <- df_udder_only |>
  filter(startsWith(event, "MAST")) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = remark_letters1,
    treatment_cat = case_when(
      startsWith(treatment, "TOD") | treatment == "TODAY"                                          ~ "Today",
      startsWith(treatment, "SP")                                                                  ~ "Spectramast",
      startsWith(treatment, "AMX")                                                                 ~ "Amoxicillin",
      startsWith(treatment, "KILL")                                                                ~ "Quarter cull",
      startsWith(treatment, "NOT") | treatment %in% c("NOTX", "CMT", "BLOOD", "DRY", "WATER",
        "BLOODY", "BLOODRR", "WATERLR", "CULL", "LF", "WAT")                                       ~ "No treatment",
      treatment %in% c("AHV", "AHVPILL")                                                           ~ "AHV",
      treatment %in% c("IV", "HYPERIV")                                                            ~ "IV support",
      treatment %in% c("PLY", "POLY")                                                              ~ "Polyflex",TRUE                                                                                         ~ "Unknown"
  ),
    dop_event_cat = factor(dop_event_cat,
      levels = c("Early_lactation", "Mid_lactation", "Late_lactation"),
      labels = c("0-21 DIM", "22-150 DIM", ">150 DIM")),
    locate_lesion_std = sapply(locate_lesion, function(x) {
      if (x == "") return("")
      chunks <- regmatches(x, gregexpr(".{2}", x))[[1]]
      paste(sort(chunks), collapse = "")
    }),
    LF = as.integer(sapply(locate_lesion_std, function(x) "LF" %in% regmatches(x, gregexpr(".{2}", x))[[1]])),
    LR = as.integer(sapply(locate_lesion_std, function(x) "LR" %in% regmatches(x, gregexpr(".{2}", x))[[1]])),
    RF = as.integer(sapply(locate_lesion_std, function(x) "RF" %in% regmatches(x, gregexpr(".{2}", x))[[1]])),
    RR = as.integer(sapply(locate_lesion_std, function(x) "RR" %in% regmatches(x, gregexpr(".{2}", x))[[1]])),
    n_quarters = case_when(
      locate_lesion_std == "" ~ "Missing",
      TRUE ~ as.character(LF + LR + RF + RR)
    )
  )

#Descriptive

df_mastitis_only |>
  count(n_quarters) |>
  arrange(n_quarters)

df_mastitis_only |>
  count(treatment_cat, treatment) |>
  arrange(treatment_cat, desc(n))

lapply(c("LF", "LR", "RF", "RR"), function(loc) {
  df_mastitis_only |>
    filter(.data[[loc]] == 1) |>
    pull(remark) |>
    unique() |>
    sort()
})

all_combinations <- c("", "LF", "LR", "RF", "RR",
  apply(combn(c("LF", "LR", "RF", "RR"), 2), 2, paste, collapse = ""),
  apply(combn(c("LF", "LR", "RF", "RR"), 3), 2, paste, collapse = ""),
  "LFLRRFRR"
)

df_mastitis_only |>
  group_by(locate_lesion_std) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(data.frame(locate_lesion_std = all_combinations), by = "locate_lesion_std") |>
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0)) |>
  arrange(locate_lesion_std)

#Quality checks

df_mastitis_only |>
  filter(locate_lesion_std == "LFLRRFRR") |>
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    without_ALL = sum(!grepl("ALL", remark, ignore.case = TRUE)),
    with_ALL = sum(grepl("ALL", remark, ignore.case = TRUE))
  )

```




Then use graphs, tables, or a combination to describe your selected events.  Has there has been a change in the treatments used over time?  Does dop (day of phase i.e. dim or age) matter for your selected events?

CAUTION: do not over think this.  I know you are all wanting to do this with a denominator to find incidence rather than raw counts.  I promise that is coming. First just get used to summarizing numerators across different groupings. 

Note: your graphics should be much prettier than the examples!! ;)



```{r}
#graph your event counts over time here.
ggplot(data = df_mastitis_only, mapping = aes(x = dop_event_cat, fill = treatment_cat)) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~ n_quarters) +
  labs(x = "DOP at event", y = "count", fill = "Treatment") +
  theme_gray()
```
